subject: Post-call: Genomex air-gapped/on-prem qualification — stakeholder matrix & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Lina Weiss <lina.weiss@genomex.com>, Mike Turner <m.turner@genomex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T15:02:00Z
Subject: Post-call: Genomex air-gapped/on-prem qualification — stakeholder matrix & next steps

Hi Lina / Mike,

Thanks again for the time today — helpful session. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Key takeaways from our discussion
- Genomex preference: leaning toward an on-prem, air-gapped appliance model for production (primary drivers: regulatory auditability and isolated PHI processing).
- Critical requirements: offline upgrade workflow, spare hardware + swap procedures, tamper-evident physical media handling, and signed binaries for any model/package updates.
- Non-functional expectations: 99.9% SLA target for inference endpoints once deployed, seasonal maintenance windows (~quarterly), and 24x7 local ops contact for initial 90 days.
- Security: KMS/HSM integration required, full audit logs, and support for customer-supplied key material.

Open questions we noted (please confirm):
1) Which rack/site will host the appliance (primary/DR)? — affects spare part staging.
2) Target maintenance window preferences (local timezone blackout periods).
3) Who is the single point of contact for change control in your ops team (name + email + pager)?

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- Action 1 (Genomex): Fill in the attached site inventory template with rack specs, network segmentation, and local storage/backups. This will let engineering size the appliance and spares correctly. (attachment: genomex-site-inventory-template.xlsx)
- Action 2 (Redwood): We will send a high-level offline-upgrade MOP and a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) within 48 business hours.
- Action 3 (Ops Sync): Schedule a 60-minute ops readiness call (ops, security, and procurement) next week to align timelines and procurement lead times for hardware/spares.

If you confirm availability, I can propose three 1-hour slots (May 3–5).

Thanks — I copied Marissa (our deployment manager) who will coordinate the MAP and PS engagement.

Cheers,

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 510-555-0147

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side before we fill the spreadsheet: 

1) Zero-trust: we need to understand how Redwood enforces mutual TLS and whether the appliance can be configured to accept only client certs issued by our internal PKI.
2) Offline upgrades: how are upgrade packages signed and delivered? Is there an option to ingest a signed tarball via USB (due to our strict outbound rules)?
3) On-site support: Would Redwood provide an on-site engineer for the initial activation and acceptance test window, or is that handled remotely?

I have attached our security questionnaire (high level) — some questions there overlap with what you covered. I will try to get the preliminary inventory back by May 5, but I need to confirm the site owner and exact rack details.

Subject: Re: Post-call: Genomex air-gapped/on-prem qualification — stakeholder matrix & next steps

Lina — great questions, answered inline below. Short version: we support PKI-based mTLS, signed upgrade artifacts, and on-site PS for initial activation (commercial engagement).

1) Mutual TLS / PKI
- The appliance supports mutual TLS with customer-provided certificates. You can configure it to trust a root CA from your internal PKI; we recommend issuing short-lived node certs for hosts.

2) Offline upgrades and signed artifacts
- All runtime and model packages are cryptographically signed by Redwood. For air-gapped installs we provide three delivery options: 
  a) SFTP to a customer-controlled DMZ host (pull),
  b) Signed tarball on encrypted USB for physical handoff,
  c) Secure courier of sealed media (for very large model bundles) with chain-of-custody docs.
- The upgrade MOP enforces signature verification and offline testing prior to cutover. See attached (redwood-offline-upgrade-mop.pdf).

3) On-site engineering and acceptance
- Redwood Professional Services can provide a field engineer for the initial 3–5 day activation and SAT (scope and rate to be quoted). Remote activation is also supported if you prefer.

Backups / restore
- We recommend local encrypted snapshots and periodic transfer to your secure object store over an air-gapped transfer mechanism (sneakernet or dedicated data diode/DMZ transfer). Restore operations are deterministic and documented in the MOP.

Proposed ops sync slots (PDT): May 3 10:00–11:00, May 4 14:00–15:00, May 5 09:00–10:00. Let me know which works and I will lock it in.

Ben
